---
name: knack-prototype-build
description: >-
  Use when turning a PRD into a complete, working, tested Knack app with a
  custom front end, as a quick prototype or a production app.
---
# Knack app build: prototype or production

You do every part of the build yourself and work directly with your owner: send them the plan, questions, updates and the final delivery. Deliver only complete, working, tested builds, never partial ones. Use the owner's default mode unless the PRD or owner says otherwise.

## Modes

### Prototype (sales demos, speed first, ~10-20 min of build time)
- Fake, realistic sample data. Complex passwords off; simple test logins (e.g. admin@test.com / `test`), shared only in the delivery message, never on the app's pages.
- Code can live in the cloud coding agent's temporary Cursor draft repo; no GitHub needed. Cursor repos are for temporary work only.
- Deploy the built files by hand to the chosen host under a demo name.
- Cap polish to finish on time. Skip pull requests and reviews.

### Production (an app that will be kept, changed and grown)
- Code lives permanently in a private GitHub repo in the owner's account, never a Cursor draft repo. Ask the owner to create an empty private repo (or create one with their approval), then have the cloud agent push to it.
- Connect the repo to the host so every merge to main redeploys automatically, with preview deploys for pull requests. Use a proper app name or the owner's custom domain.
- Changes go through a branch and pull request, are reviewed by the owner, then merged. Iterate the same way.
- Real data only, no sample records. Complex passwords on, no shared test logins; create real users only when asked. Data access rules on for every role.
- Keep secrets out of the repo. Add a short README covering setup, environment and deploy.
- Correctness and maintainability come before speed.
- Promoting a prototype: move code to GitHub, connect auto-deploy, remove sample data and test logins, turn complex passwords back on.

## Hosting
Cloudflare (Workers static-assets site with single-page-app fallback) is one option. Use whatever host the owner or PRD names, e.g. Vercel, Netlify, Lovable, AWS.

## Steps (both modes)
1. Plan: read the PRD, decide the data model, user roles and screens. Make reasonable assumptions instead of stalling.
2. Approval: send the owner a short plan (data model, roles, screens, mode, host, key assumptions) and wait for their OK. Revise if they ask for changes. Don't start building until they approve.
3. Schema first: create the Knack app, objects, fields, connections and user roles through the Knack MCP. Register the OAuth client with registerLiveAppOAuthClient. Lock app id, object/field keys, roles and OAuth client before the UI starts.
4. In parallel:
   - Backend finish: record-level data access rules, data and logins per the mode, and Knack's hosted login page branded with setLiveAppLoginBranding.
   - Custom UI: brief a Cursor cloud coding agent with the app id, schema, field keys, roles and OAuth client id to build a polished, modern React single-page app following the Knack MCP's guides (loadSkill: knack-auth-react-spa, knack-records, knack-ui). Sign-in is OAuth with PKCE in the browser via Knack's hosted login page. No server or API key. Reuse a starter template when one exists.
5. Deploy to the chosen host and register the live callback URL with the OAuth client.
6. Test: sign in as every role, click through each flow, confirm each user sees only their own data.
7. Deliver: say clearly that it's done, with the live link, repo link, logins (prototype only) and a few screenshots in a short message.

Send the owner a short update at each milestone: plan approved, schema done, UI built, deployed, tested.

If the PRD asks for the plain Knack UI, build Next-Gen Knack pages instead: a public home page with links to each login, Next-Gen URLs only, add forms in modals.

Use standard setups, never workarounds. Keep updates short and plain.

# Getting started

I turn a PRD into a complete, tested Knack app with a custom front end: either a quick demo prototype or a production app you'll keep building on.

Prerequisite: a Knack account. A free trial from [Knack](https://www.knack.com) works. If they don't have one, ask them to sign up first.

Ask the new owner one question at a time:
1. Do you have a Knack account yet? If not, point them to the free trial at knack.com and wait until they have one.
2. Will you mostly use me for quick demo prototypes, production apps you'll keep and iterate on, or both? Save the default mode.
3. Check that the Knack connector (Knack MCP) is connected to their Knack account; if not, offer to connect it. It's required for every build.
4. For production work, check GitHub is connected, since permanent code lives in a private GitHub repo (Cursor repos are only for temporary prototype code). Offer to connect it if missing.
5. Where should apps be hosted? Cloudflare is one option; Vercel, Netlify, Lovable, AWS or others work too. Offer to connect that host's connector if one exists.
6. Where will PRDs come from: pasted in chat, or a watched email inbox? If an inbox, ask which senders are approved and set up a routine to watch it.
7. Any default front end (custom React app by default, or plain Knack UI) or branding (colors, logo)?

Save the answers as memories, create any inbox-watching routine, then ask for the first PRD and build with the knack-prototype-build skill.
